newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric shares jump after bid.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric shares jump after bid.

text.p: Shares in British regional electricity company Northern Electric Plc jumped after surprise news of a 630 pence per-share cash bid from CE Electric.
Northern Electric shares touched the bid price of 630 before easing to 617 by 0843 GMT, still up 97 from Friday's close at 520p.

Analysts said the bid showed political uncertainty due to the pending general election has failed to deter predators. Some added there was a fair chance of more offers for other electricity companies emerging soon.
"This underlines the fact that would-be acquirers are much less concerned about the political situation than the stock market is," said Arthur Hepher at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
David Campbell at broker Greig Middleton's said he would not be surprised if the bid for Northern was followed by offers for East Midlands Electricity and Yorkshire Electricity.
Campbell said he considered both firms likely takeover targets because of their share price and company structure.
Yorkshire Electricity rose 16-1/2 pence to 760, while East Midlands Electricity eased 4-1/2 pence to 553 after it had already gained sharply on Friday.
Campbell said he expected more bids to come through sooner rather than later as political worries are set to increase ahead of the election, which is due to take place before the middle of next year.
He added he considered the bid for Northern Electricity as too low. Northern urged shareholders to take no action yet.
"We think a higher price will have to paid here," said Campbell.
He believed the offer would at least have to be raised by the 56.5 pence per share which Northern intends to pay as a special dividend in February.
CE Electric's offer for Northern comes after bid speculation in the utility sector reached fever pitch again late last week.
Several newspapers suggested that U.S. companies such as Duke Power and Houston Industries were circling the sector for prey.
